title: Coronavirus devastates agriculture: Dumped milk, euthanized livestock
主要内容: The coronavirus pandemic has severely impacted the U.S. agriculture sector, leading to widespread issues such as dumped milk, euthanized livestock, and discarded crops. Long & Scott Farms, a Florida-based farm, faced a significant drop in demand for its cucumbers, which are typically used in restaurants. As a result, many of these cucumbers were discarded or left to rot in fields. Similarly, farmers in South Florida reported throwing away crops due to reduced demand in stores and restaurants. The situation has also affected livestock, with pork-processing plant closures leading to overcrowding in barns and discussions about euthanizing thousands of hogs. Tyson Foods, a major player in the industry, warned that plant closures would result in the loss of millions of animals. Dairy farmers, in particular, have been struggling with weak demand, with estimates suggesting up to 3.7 million gallons of milk are being dumped daily. The U.S. Agriculture Department has established a coordination center to assist livestock and poultry producers affected by these disruptions. Additionally, chicken processors have had to euthanize chickens due to staffing shortages and reduced processing capacity. Poultry farmers like Kerry and Barb Mergen in Albany, Minnesota, faced the difficult decision of euthanizing their flock due to the economic downturn caused by the virus. Only 15 hens managed to survive the process, highlighting the scale of the crisis. Meanwhile, mushroom farmer Matt Sicher in Lenhartsville, Pennsylvania, has lost revenue from restaurants in New York City, prompting a shift from wholesale to retail sales. The beef industry also suffered as slaughterhouse closures disrupted supply chains, with many meat-processing plants becoming virus hotspots. Despite these challenges, the U.S. government took steps to keep meat-processing plants operational through an executive order signed by President Trump. These events underscore the broader impact of the pandemic on food production and distribution.
